brief.headline: The prompt premium is gone: the 05-Aug official settled cash $3,229.00 (-$42.00, -1.28%) against a 3M of $3,229.50, flipping the cash-3M structure from a +$34.50 BACKWARDATION into a $0.50 CONTANGO in a single session, after Iran and Oman agreed the geographical coordinates of a temporary Strait of Hormuz shipping route - while exchange stock drew a 26th consecutive session to 259,400 t and broke below 260,000 t for the first time.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. Cash $3,229.00, down $42.00 (-1.28%) from $3,271.00; 3M $3,229.50, down only $7.00 (-0.22%) from $3,236.50; stock 259,400 t, down 1,500 t, a 26th consecutive draw and -49.1% year-to-date. The prompt did almost all of the falling. That collapsed the cash-3M premium from +$34.50 to MINUS $0.50 - the curve is now flat to marginally in CONTANGO for the first time in this advance, having been in backwardation for the whole of the Gulf-disruption leg.

WHY IT MATTERS. Iran's Foreign Ministry confirmed on 05-Aug that Tehran and Muscat have agreed the geographical coordinates of a proposed commercial shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, with a joint statement in final review and drafting. The terms are narrower than the headline: Iran's deputy foreign minister says BOTH existing lanes - the northern lane under Iranian control and the southern lane near Oman - would close, replaced by a new transit model unlike anything of the past 60 years, and the new passage is TEMPORARY, expected to be usable for two to four months. Tehran stated explicitly that the agreement does not mean safe navigation is restored. Brent held near $79-80 after roughly 5% falls in each of the two preceding sessions.

WHAT THE CURVE IS SAYING, AND THE DIVERGENCE INSIDE IT. A prompt premium that vanishes while the warehouse keeps draining is an unusual pairing and should be stated plainly rather than smoothed: the spread says the scramble for immediate metal has stopped, the stock series says physical availability has not improved. The cleanest reading is that the spread priced the RISK of not getting metal through the corridor, and a credible routing agreement - even a temporary, partial one - removes that risk premium without adding a single tonne. The flat price barely moved on the 3M leg, which is consistent: forward supply expectations changed far less than prompt anxiety did.

WHAT TO WATCH. Whether a published transit count actually recovers - Kpler recorded just eight vessels through the strait on 05-Aug (five tankers, three bulk carriers) and 106 crossings by 96 distinct vessels over 27-Jul to 02-Aug, about 15 a day against 130-140 pre-war, so the agreement has not yet moved the observable; whether the contango persists or the backwardation re-establishes on today's 13:20-London official; whether the stock draw survives the removal of the corridor-risk bid; and the mid-August anode, CPC and coal-tar-pitch settlement cycle, which now prices against much cheaper crude than a week ago.

Convention: cash > 3M is backwardation; cash < 3M is contango. THIS IS THE HEADLINE STRUCTURAL CHANGE ON THE BOARD AND IT SITS IN DIRECT TENSION WITH THE STOCK SERIES, which drew a 26th consecutive session on the same day. A spread that goes flat while inventory keeps falling is most consistent with the withdrawal of a corridor-risk premium rather than with a resolution of physical tightness. One session does not establish a regime; the test is whether today's 13:20-London official confirms the contango or re-establishes backwardation.

lme.commentary: THE SESSION IN ONE LINE: the prompt was repriced, the forward was not. Cash fell $42.00 (-1.28%) to $3,229.00 while the 3-month fell $7.00 (-0.22%) to $3,229.50, collapsing a +$34.50 backwardation into a $0.50 contango. Every part of that move is concentrated at the front of the curve. THE TRIGGER IS DATED AND PUBLIC. On 05-Aug Iran's Foreign Ministry said Tehran and Muscat had agreed the geographical coordinates of a proposed commercial shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, with a joint statement in final review and drafting. Iran's deputy foreign minister described the mechanics: both the northern Iranian-controlled lane and the southern Omani lane would close, replaced by a new transit model unlike the past 60 years, temporary and expected to be usable for two to four months. Tehran stressed the agreement does not mean safe navigation is restored. This is materially more concrete than the disputed 02-Aug claims, and materially narrower than a reopening. THE WAREHOUSE DISAGREED WITH THE SPREAD. Stock drew a 26th consecutive session to 259,400 t, -1,500 t, through 260,000 t for the first time and roughly -49.1% year-to-date. Physical availability on exchange did not improve on the day the prompt premium disappeared. The most coherent reconciliation is that the backwardation was pricing the RISK of metal not moving rather than the ABSENCE of metal, and a credible routing agreement removes that risk at a stroke without delivering a tonne. THE OBSERVABLE HAS NOT MOVED YET. Kpler recorded eight vessels transiting the strait on 05-Aug - five tankers and three bulk carriers - and 106 crossings by 96 distinct vessels over the week 27-Jul to 02-Aug, about 15 a day against roughly 130-140 before the war began on 28-February. Transit counts, not communiques, are what would convert this from a sentiment repricing into a supply event, and they have not yet. CROSS-CHECK ON THE BOARD: the whole 05-Aug LME board is internally consistent and on one uniform session. Copper cash eased to $14,167.50 from $14,195.00, nickel fell to $16,915.00 from $17,125.00, zinc firmed to $3,737.00 and lead eased to $1,845.00, with stocks and all three EUR/USD fixings rolling together onto 05-Aug on the German overview page while the English page was still serving 04-Aug.

THE NEGOTIATING BACKDROP SWUNG BACK TOWARD BUYERS THIS RUN, HAVING SWUNG TO SELLERS LAST RUN, AND THE SWING IS NOW EVIDENCE-BASED RATHER THAN RHETORICAL. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman confirmed on 05-Aug that Tehran and Muscat have agreed the geographical coordinates of a proposed commercial shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, with a joint statement in final review and drafting after two months of technical, legal, security and environmental talks. Iran's deputy foreign minister set out the mechanics: BOTH existing lanes - the northern lane under Iranian control and the southern lane near Oman - would close, replaced by a transit model unlike anything of the past 60 years, and the new passage is TEMPORARY, expected to be usable for two to four months. Tehran stated explicitly that the agreement does NOT mean safe navigation through the strait is restored. The observable has not moved yet: Kpler recorded eight vessels transiting on 05-Aug (five tankers, three bulk carriers) and 106 crossings by 96 distinct vessels over 27-Jul to 02-Aug, about 15 a day against roughly 130-140 before the war began on 28-February. FOR THE BUYERS, the LME curve did the arguing: the prompt backwardation that underpinned the spot-squeeze case collapsed from +$34.50 to a $0.50 CONTANGO on the 05-Aug official, and the yen remains materially firmer after the first joint US-Japan intervention since 2011. FOR THE SELLERS, the physical evidence is unchanged: exchange stock is at 259,400 t after 26 consecutive draws and has broken below 260,000 t, EGA had 89 of 1,262 pots running at 02-Jul, and Alba's 04-Aug Q2 disclosure confirms it is still running 'disciplined production curtailments' with Lines 1-3 (19% of 1,623,000 t/y) offline since 15-Mar. A temporary two-to-four-month routing does not restart a potline.

Billet premiums carry the duty-paid structure plus the conversion spread over P1020, so they move with both metal availability and extruder order books, and European extrusion demand remains the soft spot in the regional balance. THE ENERGY RELIEF LASTED ONE SESSION: TTF gas rose 4.30% to about EUR 59.98/MWh on 04-Aug after falling 4.23% to EUR 56.57 on 03-Aug, so the gas curve is back near where it started a month that has run roughly 36-37% higher. Hydro's Slovalco agreement with the Slovak government to resume 75,000 t from Q4-2026 remains the first concrete European restart of the cycle and was re-confirmed in public market commentary this run; cheaper power was the condition under which others would follow, and that condition has not been met. The US premium is overwhelmingly a TARIFF construct rather than a scarcity signal: at the 04-Aug cash official of $3,271.00 the 50% Section 232 rate on aluminium articles is $1,635.50/t on its own, up $5.50 from Monday's $1,630.00 purely because the metal price rose. The 20-Jul-2026 proclamation allowing companies with an approved plan to build or expand a US primary smelter (construction beginning by 20-Jan-2029) to import at HALF the applicable rate against expected output remains the main identified route to compression, and no CBP implementing guidance has been issued yet.

drivers.text: IRAN AND OMAN AGREED THE COORDINATES OF A TEMPORARY HORMUZ SHIPPING ROUTE ON 05-AUG - AND THE LME PROMPT PREMIUM DISAPPEARED THE SAME DAY, FROM +$34.50 BACKWARDATION TO A $0.50 CONTANGO — Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman confirmed on 05-Aug that Tehran and Muscat have agreed the geographical coordinates of a proposed commercial shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, with a joint statement in final review and drafting after two months of technical, legal, security and environmental talks. Iran's deputy foreign minister set out the mechanics: BOTH existing lanes - the northern lane under Iranian control and the southern lane near Oman - would close, replaced by a transit model unlike anything of the past 60 years, and the new passage is TEMPORARY, expected to be usable for two to four months. Tehran stated explicitly that the agreement does NOT mean safe navigation through the strait is restored. The observable has not moved yet: Kpler recorded eight vessels transiting on 05-Aug (five tankers, three bulk carriers) and 106 crossings by 96 distinct vessels over 27-Jul to 02-Aug, about 15 a day against roughly 130-140 before the war began on 28-February. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT FOR THE PREMIUM COMPLEX SINCE THE DISRUPTION BEGAN, and it is materially more concrete than the disputed 02-Aug claims that unravelled inside 48 hours: this is Tehran's own foreign ministry confirming an agreed technical output, not a third-party characterisation. Every regional premium row carries a Gulf-risk component, and the LME curve repriced that component to zero on the day. drivers.text: THE PUBLISHED TRANSIT COUNT IS THE TEST AND IT HAS NOT MOVED: EIGHT VESSELS THROUGH THE STRAIT ON 05-AUG, AND ABOUT 15 A DAY OVER THE LATEST FULL WEEK AGAINST 130-140 PRE-WAR — Kpler data reported publicly show eight vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz on 05-Aug - five tankers and three bulk carriers, six inbound and two outbound - and, over the latest complete week of 27-Jul to 02-Aug, 106 crossings by 96 distinct vessels, just over 15 crossings a day. Before the war began on 28-February roughly 130-140 ships transited daily. Crude flows through the Omani lane are estimated at 3-5 million barrels a day. THIS IS THE OBSERVABLE THIS BOARD HAS BEEN ASKING FOR SINCE THE FIRST DIPLOMATIC HEADLINES, and it says the corridor is still operating at roughly a tenth of normal commercial throughput. The premium complex prices delivered metal, not communiques; until the count recovers, the physical cost of moving Gulf tonnes has not fallen.
drivers.source: Foreign Policy Journal / Kpler - Strait of Hormuz crossings rise 8% week-on-week (03-Aug-2026)

THE CHINA READ IS DIVERGING FROM THE EX-CHINA READ. SMM's most recent free alumina commentary continues to describe a market in the doldrums with cost support wrestling weak demand, port inventory building on high overseas arrivals and the oversupply pattern unchanged, and SMM's stated precondition for any bullish driver - implementation of Guinea's bauxite quota policy - has still not been met. Against that, the 05-Aug transaction of 30,000 mt at $356/mt FOB East Australia for September loading is a firm ex-China print that does not fit the doldrums framing. SMM puts the Chinese industry average full cost near 2,530 yuan/mt on Guinea bauxite at $70-75/mt, so the Chinese contract remains only a few per cent above its cost floor while the seaborne market is transacting higher. Watch whether that gap pulls Chinese prices up or seaborne prices back.

THE POLICY VARIABLE IS NOW THE MARKET'S STATED SWING FACTOR: SMM's 04-Aug alumina brief says explicitly that 'before Guinea's bauxite quota policy is implemented, the market lacks clear bullish drivers' - a 2026 Guinea export cap near 150 Mt has been considered but NOT implemented, and its implementation is the single identified route out of the current oversupply. Against that, oversupply remains structural: Guinea shipped a RECORD 114.8 Mt in H1-2026, +15% y/y, and China's alumina imports ran +749% y/y to 2.28 Mt in H1 with 91.7% of it Australian. SMM's 02-Aug inventory note recorded bauxite stocks at ten Chinese ports falling 730,000 mt week-on-week as at 31-Jul, the first materially tighter port read of the cycle; the 04-Aug brief adds that ALUMINA port inventory continued to BUILD on high overseas arrivals. notes: Alumina is roughly 1.92 t per tonne of aluminium and typically 30-40% of smelter cash cost, so it is the single largest determinant of where the industry cost curve sits and therefore of how far the metal price can fall before supply responds. At the carried $328/t FOB Western Australia against a 05-Aug LME 3M of $3,229.50, alumina is about 10.2% of the metal price; on the 05-Aug transacted $356/t FOB East Australia basis it would be about 11.0%. The ratio rose this run for the first time in a fortnight, and it rose from both directions - the metal fell and the freshest seaborne evidence firmed.

THE NEW DATAPOINT THIS RUN IS A PHYSICAL TRADE, NOT AN ASSESSMENT. SMM reported that on 05-Aug-2026 30,000 mt of alumina transacted at $356/mt FOB East Australia for September loading. That is a dated, publicly reported transaction, which is a harder form of evidence than a carried assessment, and it sits above every other ex-China reference on this table - the 09-Jul SMM WA assessment at $328, the 01-Aug CME FOB Australia futures settlement at $333.34 and the 26-Jun Platts FOB Australia mark at $330. The port basis differs and that is stated rather than blended away, but the direction is unambiguous.

THE PRECISE CURRENT SMM CHINA INDEX LEVEL IS NOT PUBLISHED HERE because it sits behind SMM's paywall; the SMM-AL-AO-002 live page again returned no free value at this refresh. The last free print of 2,730.17 yuan/mt is carried at 16-Jul-2026 and the date was deliberately NOT upgraded. SMM's free commentary continues to describe Chinese alumina as being in the doldrums, with cost support wrestling weak demand and port inventory building on high overseas arrivals. THE MARKS ON THIS TABLE ARE OF DIFFERENT VINTAGES AND EACH ROW STATES ITS OWN: the 05-Aug physical transaction is the freshest; the CME FOB Australia futures line is carried unchanged at 01-Aug; SMM's FOB Western Australia assessment is carried at 09-Jul; the Platts FOB Australia mark at 26-Jun is stale at 41 days.

COMMERCIAL LOGIC - THE MARGIN SQUEEZE NOW HAS TWO BLADES. Cheap alumina against a high LME is why the July earnings season was uniformly strong across the producer set: Alcoa's Aluminum segment posted record EBITDA at a 32.3% margin, Hydro beat on adjusted EBITDA, Vedanta ran a 48.1% margin, and Alba's 04-Aug Q2 disclosure showed $295m EBITDA with profit up 164% year-on-year while running curtailed. This run, for the first time in the cycle, both blades moved against that: the metal's prompt premium vanished into contango AND the freshest seaborne alumina evidence firmed to $356/t. Neither move is yet large enough to threaten margins that wide, but the direction has changed. logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THE FIRST CONCRETE DIPLOMATIC OUTPUT OF THE CRISIS, AND IT IS NARROWER THAN THE HEADLINE. On 05-Aug Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman said Tehran and Muscat had agreed the geographical coordinates of a proposed commercial shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, with a joint statement in final review and drafting after two months of technical, legal, security and environmental talks. Iran's deputy foreign minister set out the mechanics: BOTH existing lanes - the northern lane under Iranian control and the southern lane near Oman - would close, replaced by a transit model unlike anything of the past 60 years; the new passage is TEMPORARY and expected to be usable for two to four months. Tehran stated explicitly that the agreement does NOT mean safe navigation through the strait is restored, and said a deal would be struck only 'if certain third parties do not obstruct this process'. A Gulf official was quoted putting the odds of an Iran-Oman deal by Friday at 50-50. THE OBSERVABLE HAS NOT MOVED. Kpler recorded eight vessels transiting on 05-Aug - five tankers and three bulk carriers, six inbound and two outbound - and 106 crossings by 96 distinct vessels over 27-Jul to 02-Aug, just over 15 a day, against roughly 130-140 before the war began on 28-February; crude flows through the Omani lane are estimated at 3-5 million barrels a day. The trend flag moves to DOWN because the risk direction has genuinely improved, but the corridor is still operating at roughly a tenth of normal commercial throughput and the agreement is time-limited by its own terms.

The Houthis claimed attacks on Aramco sites at Jizan and Yanbu, prompting Saudi Arabia to divert crude exports to the Suez routing. With both Gulf chokepoints impaired simultaneously, the freight and insurance wedge compounds on Gulf-origin metal and on Suez-routed alumina and semis alike. UPDATE 06-AUG: the Red Sea leg is NOT following Hormuz. Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen claimed on 05-Aug that they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, and a ship was reported hit in the Red Sea on the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address the Bab al Mandeb constraint, so the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes remains impaired and the two chokepoints are now diverging for the first time since the escalation.

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance

Around 90% of ocean-going tonnage covered by the International Group of P&I Clubs faces cancellation-and-repricing clauses on short notice. THIS IS THE SLOWEST-MOVING PART OF THE DELIVERED-COST STACK AND IT MOVES ONLY ON REALISED LOSSES - which is why it did not fall on Monday's announcement of talks and has not risen on Tuesday's denial of them, but why each new incident resets the underwriters' loss experience upward. The loss record extended again this run with a cargo vessel reported struck near the strait's Omani coast on 04-Aug, after the 01-Aug tanker strike near Lima, Oman and a second incident north-east of Khasab. Even on a signed agreement, the insurance wedge is likely to persist for months, putting a floor under Gulf-origin delivered costs independent of the LME price.

SMM's 06-Aug brief records Chinese aluminium social inventory down 25,000 t from Monday to 933,000 t and down 20,000 t week-on-week as ingot destocking recovered, with cast aluminium alloy ingot inventory down a tenth consecutive week to 24,000 t. SHFE aluminium 2609 closed 23,835 yuan/mt, up 70 yuan (+0.29%), and SMM expects prices to consolidate on a strong note. The two exchanges moved in opposite directions on the same session, which is itself evidence that the LME move was geopolitics-specific.

NOVELIS REPORTED Q1 FY27 AHEAD OF PARENT HINDALCO: net income $164m (+71% year-on-year), adjusted EBITDA $516m (+24%) and net sales $5.8bn (+23%). The downstream read-across is that rolled-products economics are expanding alongside upstream rather than being squeezed by a high metal price. Hindalco's own Q1 FY27 board meeting is 07-Aug, with management having guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation - so the upstream test is still to come.

US CONSULTS ON WIDENING SECTION 232 COVERAGE. The Department of Commerce published a Federal Register notice seeking public comment on bringing 14 further derivative products - including aluminium powder, welder parts and tank semi-trailers - inside the Section 232 scope for steel, aluminium and copper, with the 50% headline rate maintained. Bullish for the US Midwest premium and for domestic producers; bearish for US downstream converters and exporters into the US. The tariff leg itself fell $21.00/t on the session by pure arithmetic, to $1,614.50/t on the 05-Aug cash official.

THE RED SEA IS NOT FOLLOWING HORMUZ. Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen claimed on 05-Aug that they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit in the Red Sea the same day. A Hormuz routing agreement does not address the Bab al Mandeb constraint, so the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes into Rotterdam remains impaired and the two chokepoints have begun to diverge for the first time since the escalation.

Holly back at full capacity for the first time since 2015.

WHETHER THE IRAN-OMAN JOINT STATEMENT IS ACTUALLY SIGNED - a Gulf official was quoted putting the odds of a deal by Friday at 50-50, and the statement is described as being in final review and drafting. Iran has said a deal happens only 'if certain third parties do not obstruct this process'. A signed statement with a start date for the new routing would be the most bearish single development available for the premium complex; a collapse of the drafting would restore the risk premium the curve gave up on 05-Aug.

HINDALCO Q1 FY27 RESULTS, board meeting 07-Aug with the call at 16:00 IST. Novelis has already reported net income of $164m (+71%), adjusted EBITDA $516m (+24%) and net sales $5.8bn (+23%), so the downstream leg is known and strong; the open question is upstream, where management has guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation and the India Aluminium Upstream EBITDA strip has risen four consecutive quarters to a record RS 5,448cr in Q4 FY26.

PUBLISHED HORMUZ TRANSIT COUNTS - now the decisive observable rather than a supporting one, because the diplomatic step has already been taken and the market has already paid for it. Kpler recorded eight vessels on 05-Aug and about 15 a day over 27-Jul to 02-Aug, against roughly 130-140 pre-war. A recovery toward pre-war levels would confirm the prompt repricing and pressure the premium complex; a flat count for another week would suggest the curve moved on an announcement that has not yet changed physical reality.

WHETHER THE 26-SESSION STOCK DRAW ENDS. Exchange stock is 259,400 t, through 260,000 t for the first time, falling at an almost mechanical 1,500-1,750 t per session. The first BUILD would be far more significant than any further draw: metal returning to warehouse alongside a persistent contango would be the clearest confirmation available that the tightness regime has ended.

SMM WEEKLY CHINA ALUMINIUM INGOT AND BILLET SOCIAL INVENTORY - the direct test of whether the resumed destocking holds. Social inventory fell 25,000 t from Monday to 933,000 t and 20,000 t week-on-week, and cast alloy ingot inventory fell a tenth consecutive week to 24,000 t, but SMM notes the destocking pace slowed sharply and attributes it to supply composition rather than demand, with the high-temperature off-season cutting cast alloy operating rates and orders.

risks.text: THE DIPLOMATIC RISK PARTLY MATERIALISED THIS RUN AND THE MARKET PAID FOR IT IMMEDIATELY - Iran's Foreign Ministry confirmed on 05-Aug that Tehran and Muscat had agreed the geographical coordinates of a proposed Hormuz shipping route, with a joint statement in final review and drafting, and the LME prompt premium collapsed from +$34.50 backwardation to a $0.50 contango on the same session. The remaining risk is the SECOND leg: a verified reopening with recovering transit counts. The June precedent stands on the official record - on the 17-Jun ceasefire the official cash fell from $3,855.00 to $3,061.50, -20.6%. What limits it is that the agreed route is temporary by Tehran's own account (two to four months), closes both existing lanes, and does not restore safe navigation.

THE PROMPT PREMIUM IS GONE AND THAT IS NOW A FACT RATHER THAN A WATCH-ITEM - the cash-3M structure went from +$48.00 on 03-Aug to +$34.50 on 04-Aug to a $0.50 CONTANGO on 05-Aug. The prior compile said a second consecutive narrowing would be the signal that matters; it came and went through zero. The remaining question is durability: a contango that holds for several sessions, especially alongside the first exchange stock BUILD in 26 sessions, would confirm the tightness regime has ended. A prompt that re-establishes backwardation on today's official would mark this as a one-day risk unwind.

SUPPLY IS RETURNING WITHOUT A DEAL AND WOULD ACCELERATE WITH ONE - outside-China daily-average output rose 1.6% month-on-month in July on Middle East and Iceland restarts even as the year-on-year comparison fell 6.7%, and the dated pipeline is real: Slovalco +75 kt from Q4-2026, the Missouri smelter by year-end, Century's Mt. Holly already back at full capacity for the first time since 2015, Marston +75 kt, Balco 168 kt (+17% y/y), and EGA still restoring Al Taweelah. Chinese operating capacity is 45.31 Mt/y against the 45 Mt cap with H1 output 22.34 Mt (+2.24% y/y). The energy relief this run makes the European leg of that pipeline cheaper to execute.

THE COST FLOOR IS FALLING AGAIN, WHICH REMOVES THE MECHANISM THAT WOULD FORCE SUPPLY DISCIPLINE ON A FALLING PRICE. Brent traded near $79-80 after falls of around 5% in each of two preceding sessions to a three-week low, and Dutch TTF fell back to about EUR 53.67/MWh from roughly EUR 59.98 - about 10% in two sessions. Power is 30-40% of smelter cash cost and crude feeds green petcoke into CPC and prebaked anodes, so the mid-August settlement cycle now prices against a cheaper feedstock. Working the other way, the freshest seaborne alumina evidence FIRMED: 30,000 mt transacted at $356/mt FOB East Australia for September loading on 05-Aug, above every carried reference. The cost curve has split again, with energy down and alumina up.

CHINESE DOWNSTREAM DEMAND REMAINS THE WEAK LINK, BUT THE CHINESE INVENTORY DATA IMPROVED THIS RUN - SMM records aluminium social inventory down 25,000 t from Monday to 933,000 t and 20,000 t week-on-week as ingot destocking resumed, with cast alloy ingot inventory down a tenth consecutive week to 24,000 t and SHFE 2609 up 0.29% to 23,835 yuan/mt. SMM still attributes the destocking to a rising liquid-aluminium share and supply contraction rather than demand pull, and flags weak traditional end-use demand in the high-temperature off-season with cast alloy operating rates falling and orders shrinking. The official NBS manufacturing PMI is in contraction at 49.2 against the private RatingDog gauge at 50.9.

THE Q4 MJP PREMIUM NEGOTIATION TILTED TOWARD BUYERS THIS RUN AND, UNLIKE THE 02-AUG TILT, IT IS BACKED BY A CURVE MOVE - the prompt backwardation that underpinned the spot-squeeze case collapsed into contango on the 05-Aug official, and the yen remains materially firmer after the first joint US-Japan intervention since 2011, with USD/JPY near 157.7. Sellers retain the harder facts: exchange stock at 259,400 t through 260,000 t after 26 draws, EGA at 89 of 1,262 pots, Alba's Lines 1-3 still shut. Talks are expected to open around late August off an 11-year-high $395/t Q3 settlement; the scenario range carried here was widened to $310-410 and is a construct, not an assessment.

EXTERNAL DEMAND CONTINUES TO OUTPERFORM THE OFFICIAL CHINA SURVEY - the private RatingDog July manufacturing PMI printed 50.9, in expansion, against NBS 49.2, with new orders up a 14th consecutive month and foreign sales rising for the first time in three. Korea 53.1, Taiwan 55.1 and Vietnam 52.9 all expanded with export orders improving. LME copper eased only $27.50 off Tuesday's fresh 2026 high on 05-Aug while its exchange stock drew a further 6,525 t to 231,825 t - copper did NOT follow aluminium's prompt collapse, which is direct evidence that the aluminium move was geopolitics-specific rather than a broad industrial-demand signal. This is a risk to the BEARISH case, not to the bullish one.

MONETARY TIGHTENING RISK EASED AT THE MARGIN THIS RUN - the dollar index slipped back below 100 to about 99.67 and the LME EUR/USD fixing firmed to 1.15530 from 1.15170, partially reversing Tuesday's hawkish-Fed dollar bid. Fed Governor Cook said this week she would support rate HIKES if disinflation does not resume and that the risk of entrenched inflation is rising, but also that there are reasons to believe inflation may ease and the Fed may ultimately not need to raise rates. The Fed held 9-3 on 29-Jul with three dissents FOR a hike; June core PCE at +0.1% m/m and 3.3% y/y leans dovish, and this week's sharp fall in crude and European gas removes part of the energy impulse working against disinflation. Decision point: the 15-16 September FOMC with dots.

THE RED SEA CONSTRAINT IS DIVERGING FROM HORMUZ AND IS NOT ADDRESSED BY THE ROUTING AGREEMENT - Houthi forces claimed on 05-Aug that they had targeted a Saudi oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden and threatened further vessels in the Red Sea, with a ship reported hit the same day. Bab al Mandeb traffic had already fallen to a weekly low of 16 commodity vessels on 26-Jul after the 20-Jul Houthi 'embargo' on Saudi shipping, recovering only to 31 by 31-Jul. The Suez leg that carries Gulf and Asian metal into Rotterdam therefore remains impaired even if Hormuz improves, which puts a floor under European delivered costs that the market may be discounting.
